means.duplicate_chapters: Merged chapters that two sources described separately
means.thin_sitemap: Replaced sitemap rows where a fuller capture of the same work existed
means.resolver: Dropped rows the catch-all reader produced that a named adapter already covered
means.samples: Held back promotional read-throughs of finished volumes as print candidates
means.discovery-candidate: Admitted works that a discovery list names
means.platform-genre: Admitted works that a platform files under its own yuri genre

invariants.name: state agrees with its own date

budgets.name: uncertain readings
budgets.means: readings assembled character by character because no analyser could read the word. A rise means new works whose kanji nothing can read, or a regression in the analyser passes.

budgets.name: works without English
budgets.means: works that render in Japanese in English-only mode. Should be 0; a rise means the automatic naming pass stopped covering something it used to.

budgets.name: works showing a romanisation
budgets.means: works with no English name, showing a romanisation instead. Distinct from the budget above, which a romanisation satisfies: this is the one that answers 'can a reader tell what this is'. Never reaches zero, because romanising is right for a coinage.

budgets.name: incomplete attested rows
budgets.means: attested releases missing a chapter name, author or access state. The classic sign of a moved CSS selector — the adapter still returns rows, just emptier ones.

budgets.name: captures with no floor
budgets.means: adapters that fetch from a host, write into data/source, and have nothing to refuse on. A host serving nonsense replaces the last good capture and reports success. adapters/ledger.py reports the damage afterwards; a floor prevents it.

budgets.name: unreadable bookwalker rows
budgets.means: rows admitted from BOOK☆WALKER's shelf with no first publication VENUE, which is what §6's scope test turns on since the 2026-08-05 amendment. A row without one has not been fetched yet, or its series page listed nothing readable. Falls as adapters/recon/bookwalker_volumes.py works through the queue, and reaches zero when it finishes. The date is deliberately not what is counted: 1,500 of these titles are digital-only, have no print edition anywhere, and are complete records without one.

budgets.name: undated cmoa candidates
budgets.means: the same count for the コミックシーモア half of the queue, falling as adapters/cmoa_volumes.py works through it. Its floor is high and known: cmoa states an ISBN or an 出版年月 only where a volume was printed, and 754 of the 1,844 rows come from two digital distributors whose pages carry neither.

budgets.name: scraped counters in chapter names
budgets.means: chapter names ending in the view or like counts printed next to them on the source page. A rise means an extractor has gone back to flattening a chapter block into one run of text instead of reading the element the page names as the title.
